title: hotfix: reduce SLO-enforcer over-shedding during regional failover
author: Aisha Khan
description:
Motivation: During a partial regional outage last week we observed the SLO enforcer entering overly-aggressive load-shedding when combined with the regional failover path. This led to unnecessary request drop rates and secondary SLO violations for downstream services. This hotfix reduces over-shedding by introducing a backoff and hysteresis to the circuit-breaker thresholds and makes the regional-failover path tolerant to transient latency spikes.

What this PR does: 1) Introduces an exponential backoff on SLO-enforcer circuit-breaker reopen attempts to avoid thrash during repeated failovers. 2) Adds a short hysteresis window (configurable) so that the enforcer requires sustained signal before shedding at high rates. 3) Adjusts default shedding aggression for regional failover routes to prefer degraded responses over hard drops. 4) Adds detailed metrics and tracing tags so ops can distinguish failover-initiated shedding from normal shedding. 5) Adds unit and integration tests (including a perf-canary test that simulates regional failover) and a rollback-safe feature flag.

Testing & rollout: staged rollout to dedicated and hosted canaries (region us-west-2 first), perf canary run for 12h with synthetic traffic spike, then gradual ramp to 50% for 2 hours before full rollout. Monitoring dashboards and alert thresholds added so we can auto-roll back if shedding exceeds target thresholds.

Checklist: - [x] Code changes + unit tests - [x] Integration + perf-canary test added - [x] Metrics/tracing added - [x] Config flag + default safe values - [x] Docs + runbook updated - [x] Smoke tested in staging

Notes: This is a hotfix and should be backported to the previous release branch (release/2026-02) after merge. Related Linear tickets: ENG-4821 (primary), ENG-4902 (follow-up to reduce default shedding further).

b2c3e91: adjust default failover shedding policy + docs and runbook
review_comments: Miguel Torres: Please add an entry in the migration notes explaining the config keys and the expected impact on dropped request counts (ACKed).
Aisha Khan: Added migration notes and a short explanation in docs/runbooks (see last commit).
Priya Patel: Can we reduce the default max backoff from 60s to 30s? Concerned about slow recovery for small blips.
Aisha Khan: Lowered default max backoff to 30s and added a config knob for operators to increase if desired.
Samir Rao (approve): Verified behavior in staging canary; metrics look good and no regression on token-per-second throughput.
testing_notes: Staging: applied to dedicated canary cluster (us-west-2) and ran perf-canary script for 12 hours with synthetic failover. Prometheus metrics added for 'slo_enforcer.shed_rate' and 'slo_enforcer.backoff_state'. No regressions in latency P95 observed. Rollout: 10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% with 30m observation windows. Rollback condition: shed_rate > configured SLO threshold for 3 consecutive windows.
release_notes: Hotfix: Adjust SLO enforcer backoff and hysteresis to prevent aggressive load-shedding during regional failover. Adds staging/perf-canary tests, metrics, and a feature flag for safe rollout. Backport to release/2026-02 recommended.
post_merge_actions: Backport to release/2026-02; schedule follow-up ENG-4902 to evaluate long-term defaults and telemetry; update customers with dedicated capacity contracts about reduced failover drops.
notes_for_oncall: If shedding spikes unexpectedly after rollout: check 'slo_enforcer.backoff_state' and 'regional_failover.active' tags. If enforcer repeatedly opens/closes within short windows, consider toggling the feature flag to revert to previous behavior and open ENG-4902 for further analysis.
